skills.trigger: When evaluating a chest X-ray showing complete opacification (white-out) of a hemithorax to determine the underlying etiology based on mediastinal position.
steps: Confirm the extent of opacification involves the entire hemithorax, obscuring the hemidiaphragm and heart border.
Assess the position of the trachea and mediastinal structures relative to the opacity.

If the mediastinum is shifted to the contralateral side (away from the opacity), identify this as a 'pushing' lesion indicative of space-occupying pathology like massive pleural effusion or large mass.
Distinguish from atelectasis (which causes ipsilateral pull) and pneumothorax (which presents as hyperlucency/black-out rather than white-out).
